newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro-bourses slip as investors take profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro-bourses slip as investors take profits.

text.p: European share markets slipped on Wednesday as investors on both sides of the Atlantic cashed in some of their recent big gains ahead of key U.S. prices data.
Wall Street failed to live up to its early promise overnight and ended five points down, but above the 6,000 point close achieved for the first time on Monday.
Its 6,004.78 finish set the early tone in Europe, where London, France and Frankfurt all went into retreat in early trading before the release of consumer inflation data in the United States.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar extended Tuesday's rally in early trading. It later eased back to just over 1.54 marks but traders said the chart picture remained very bullish.

Oil markets traded near six-year highs on Tuesday and could squeeze even higher if the northern hemisphere winter proves severe and Iraq is unable to return to the world market, former OPEC secretary-general Subroto said.
Benchmark November Brent crude was trading just under $25 a barrel in early European trade after breaking through the key level on Monday.
British shares rapidly lost ground with government bonds during the morning after higher-than-expected figures for government borrowing.
Shares retreated from Tuesday's record close of 4,050.8 from the start, the FTSE 100 slipping 17 points to 4,033 by 0930 GMT.

The British market has advanced around 11 percent since July. But talk of a sharp correction has subsided somewhat as shares have pushed upward from the 4,000 level and as the economic background has continued to remain supportive.
German shares also opened bourse trade lower, reflecting late profit-taking in Tuesday's electronic trade and a similar mood on Wall Street.
As the DAX slipped around 15 points, VW was the only significant gainer, buoyed by strong General Motors results that were seen indicating strength in the motor sector.
French stocks opened stable but slipped about seven points in early business.
Equity and foreign exchange traders said they were waiting for U.S. consumer inflation figures for September at 1230 GMT for fresh direction.
"The dollar looks fairly well underpinned now at this point and will probably wait for the CPI report for its next cue," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economic adviser at Bank of America.
Analysts polled by Reuters expected a 0.3 percent rise in the headline CPI figure for September.

"In some respects it is a no-lose situation for the dollar here because if it's a modest number, asset markets will rise again and, if not, the prospect of higher U.S. interest rates should also buoy the currency," Hawkins said.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
At 0930 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.5409 marks and 112.08 yen, compared with 1.5394 marks and 112.29 yen in late European business on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
London - The FTSE index was down 17.2 points at 4,033.6.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 15.16 points at 2,713.29.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was down 7.51 points at 2,160.77. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $380.80 against $381.00 on Tuesday. Silver was one cent lower at $5.02.
